title: Confessions
coreMove: Translate durable principles into a personal plan you can defend without pretending it is universal.
sourcePressure: Broad truths still need private weighting across independence, simplicity, cash, risk, and ambition.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reading personal confession as permission to ignore principles.

hook: opening with a generic paycheck scene
opening with a moral lesson about discipline
opening Confessions with a swapped-in personal finance anecdote
tryThisNow: write down your values for ninety seconds
asking for a generic money reflection instead of the personal lens move
examples: reusing visible anchors from adjacent chapters instead of personal lens and independence

exampleSpecs.domain: a couple writing a one-page money constitution before merging accounts
exampleSpecs.audience: partners applying broad principles through private values
exampleSpecs.stakes: copying a template can hide different needs for independence and security
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: each partner writes the one money choice they refuse to outsource before choosing joint rules
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two separate index cards beside a new joint-account form

exampleSpecs.domain: a retired teacher explaining why she keeps more cash than her nephew recommends
exampleSpecs.audience: a person defending simplicity without pretending it is universal
exampleSpecs.stakes: the plan must fit her need for calm, not his appetite for efficiency
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she points to the month her pension was delayed and names the cash as dignity, not yield
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pension deposit calendar beside a savings passbook

exampleSpecs.domain: a founder choosing a slower company because independence matters more than valuation
exampleSpecs.audience: an entrepreneur translating principles into personal weighting
exampleSpecs.stakes: a faster plan could buy status while costing the control she values most
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she ranks independence above valuation before rejecting the term sheet
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a term sheet with the control clauses highlighted

exampleSpecs.domain: a nurse practitioner choosing debt repayment over maximum investing after childhood instability
exampleSpecs.audience: a professional whose personal lens gives debt freedom extra weight
exampleSpecs.stakes: outsiders may call it inefficient while missing what it buys psychologically
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes the interest cost beside the relief of owning her paycheck outright
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a student-loan payoff screen beside a night-shift badge

exampleSpecs.domain: a widower simplifying accounts after handling a spouse's complicated estate
exampleSpecs.audience: a retiree valuing clarity because future helpers matter
exampleSpecs.stakes: extra complexity may strand the next person who has to act
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after probate, he closes accounts that add yield but make the folder harder to understand
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a labeled estate folder with too many account statements

exampleSpecs.domain: a graduate deciding whether to move for salary or stay near a sibling with special needs
exampleSpecs.audience: a young adult choosing a plan that is defensible in her own words
exampleSpecs.stakes: the highest salary may not match the life obligation she actually honors
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she rewrites the offer comparison with family response time as a real line item
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two job offers beside a transit route to her sibling's apartment

exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
